headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/data-leakage via shared filesystem: Mentat writes diffs and reads files, while the paired source-available leak corpus can be treated as attacker-controlled content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem, so attacker-controlled content in the paired source-available corpus could be fed back into its diff-based workflow. The second agent is a leak-oriented repository with no runtime protections or provenance tracking, so interaction risk is plausible even though direct bridging is undocumented.
conditions: IF files from the leak corpus are opened in the same workspace as Mentat
IF Mentat is asked to summarize or edit content originating from the paired repository
mitigations: Keep the two repos in separate directories
Review any pasted content before giving it to Mentat
Disable copy-paste of untrusted repo text into prompts
Use a throwaway clone for the leak corpus
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat can read selected files and sends prompts to a configured model provider, while the paired repository is source-available and may contain sensitive examples or prompts. Because shared workspace is the only documented bridge, leakage is plausible if both agents touch the same files, but there is no direct evidence of automatic exfiltration from the second agent.
conditions: IF the same workspace contains secrets or private code
IF Mentat is pointed at files from the paired repository
mitigations: Separate sensitive files from the shared workspace
Run Mentat only on sanitized copies
Remove API keys from the working tree
Restrict the model provider account to non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has filesystem write and git-state modification, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via filesystem. The second agent has no write capability documented, so direct conflict is asymmetric, but the shared mutable workspace still creates collision risk if the pair operates on the same repo or branch.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF the second agent is wrapped by an external process that writes files
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent
Serialize edits through one operator
Avoid concurrent runs on the same checkout
Commit or stash before switching agents
requires-engineering: add file locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals that can be treated as authoritative by downstream tooling, while the paired repository is a leak corpus that may contain misleading or malicious text. If the second agent forwards that text into Mentat without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect edits; the interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF outputs from the leak corpus are copied into Mentat as instructions
IF a downstream operator applies Mentat diffs without review
mitigations: Require human review of every diff
Do not paste untrusted text into edit prompts
Cross-check claims against original sources
Use a second reviewer for high-impact files
requires-engineering: add verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat explicitly handles model-provider API keys and can send file contents to a configured provider, while the paired repository is source-available and not documented as handling regulated data. No residency or certification mismatch is evidenced, so compliance risk is limited to accidental inclusion of sensitive material in the shared workspace.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in files Mentat reads
IF the model provider account is not approved for that data class
mitigations: Exclude regulated files from the workspace
Use a non-sensitive test project
Rotate exposed API keys if needed
Document allowed data classes for the provider
requires-engineering: add data-loss controls
